blind.why: Arc fire (FP) vs real CS:GO-era ak47_01.wav (isolated, from github RoyZ-iwnl/spray.training). Same chart format: waveform, spectrogram, 5 ms RMS envelope. I picked B for its clean instant onset and smooth decay; A had a ragged double peak at 0.16 s. A was the real AK. The real shot is denser (crest 10 dB) with a longer tail (T-40 726 ms vs ours 391 ms).
Pip vs cz75_01. B had a cleaner single transient. The real pistol has a sustained 50 ms burst plus body. Pip's crest is 23.5 dB vs 13.9 dB, so ours is a spike: -28.9 LUFS-s at -1.5 dBFS peak.

Zip vs mac10_01. I picked the crisp 15 ms spike (ours) over the 250 ms dense report (real). On reflection that spike is the 'thin' problem: Zip drops -20 dB in 16 ms vs 94 ms for the real gun. A 4th pair (Arc reload1 vs ak47_clipout) also went to ours, because the real file is truncated at 0.19 s. Charts reward tidiness, so I give these wins little weight.

biggest_gap: Your own gunfire goes silent mid-spray. In mixer.js:80 the per-sound voice cap (tagger.<id>.fire voices=8, or MAXV) has no voice stealing: a new instance is simply dropped, even first-person prio-3 shots. setTimeout disposal keeps each voice ~V.end+0.6 s (about 1.6 s for Arc), and the cap is shared with every bot using the same tagger. Repro: node shots/critic-audio-r2/spray.mjs (real-time AudioContext, ?scene=sound-lab, ctx.audio.play FP at the weapon's rpm, 30 shots). Arc is silent on 10/30 shots (seq 111111110000011111111000011011), Rail 8/30, Storm 7/30. In the real match (shots/critic-audio-r2/duel.mjs) 21 consecutive local tagger.arc.fire calls returned null (DROPPED) at 23.4-27.7 s. CS2 never loses the local player's shot. Fix: exempt fp/local from the cap or steal the oldest/quietest voice of that name, count local and remote separately, and shorten the hold to the audible tail.
other_gaps: Pistol/SMG reports are spikes, not shots. Pip FP is -28.9 LUFS-s with 23.5 dB crest; Zip/Hum/Twin crest is 18-20 dB with T-20 of 16-38 ms. Real CS: crest 10-14 dB, T-20 44-235 ms. The default pistol sounds quieter than hit.crown (-24) and util pops (-22). Add a sustained 30-80 ms body/mechanical layer and raise Pip ~6 LU.

Hit confirm still buried: hit.tick is -31.6 LUFS-s vs Arc fire -20.3, about 11 LU under the shot and barely above impacts (-35). dmg.taken has a 66 Hz centroid and tag.out.self 165 Hz (pure sub), so both are inaudible on laptop speakers or earbuds. Give them 1-3 kHz content.

Footstep information is weak. With step.stone TP at 8 m the broadband ILD is only 4.9 dB at 90°. Level is -46 LUFS at 3 m, -56 at 8 m and -62 at 16 m, with a hard cutoff by 50 m. One occluder costs -9 to -11 dB and drops the centroid from 3030 to 553 Hz, so a step 10 m behind a thin wall comes out at -69 LUFS (inaudible). CS2 keeps occluded steps audible and directional.

Third-person gunfire turns dark. Arc at 10/30/60 m has a 480/545/518 Hz centroid. At 25 m TP, Arc/Rail/Judge/Storm/Lance are 218-584 Hz, so the weapon is hard to identify by ear at range. FP Judge is still 109 Hz (97% of energy below 300 Hz). The closest TP feature pairs are arc~storm 5.0 dB and judge~storm 5.2 dB. The closest FP pair is twin~hum at 4.3 dB, while the closest CS pair is mac10~mp9 at 5.8 dB.

Music is close to inaudible and still seams. Menu -44.6, buy -47.6, live -53, win sting -40 LUFS (rifle -20, VO -31.5). music.menu jumps +20 dB within 10 ms at every bar line (2.91/5.77/8.63 s), the pad retrigger seam from r1. Armed drops to -75 dB between hits.
Announcer is -31.5 LUFS, 11 LU under rifle fire. It is a formant buzz with a broadband click 80 ms in. It should sit around -23 so callouts survive a firefight.
Ping is played positionally for every 'ping' event (events.js:134) with no team filter. Verify that enemy pings are not audible (in the match, 36 ui.ping played for 35 ping events, mostly from bots).
bugs: Local FP gunfire dropped by the voice cap (see biggest_gap). 33% of an Arc spray is silent in real time.

Renderer intermittently hung or crashed during tools/audio_dump.mjs (the --tp pass stalled after tagger.judge.reload1 and tagger.pickup, then later 'Target crashed' on ui.round.*/announce.*). Likely machine load, but a hang with no timeout makes the tool unreliable.
strengths: FP gunfire is far brighter than in r1. Arc/Rail/Pip/Twin/Zip centroids are 0.9-3.3 kHz, and variants decorrelate like real CS samples (spectral corr 0.91 vs 0.90-0.91 between real m4a1_01/02).
Level ladder is mostly in order: rifles -20 > hit.crown/kill -24/-23 > impacts -35 > steps -38 > UI -40..-44.

r1 wiring bugs fixed: a single roundStart VO per round; inspect, scoreboard, ping, whiz, dmg.taken, hit.crown/kill, beacon beeps, 10 s/5 VO and horn all fire in a real bot match with no console errors.
Front/back HF shading on steps (+7.4 dB tilt in front vs +2.8 dB behind) and a working occlusion LPF.
Reload stages have slide + clack structure with real low-frequency mass.
